title: Micropolar cavity: centre lines with the two Newtonian bounds, fields, the slab cut
status: final (rc2 runs), incomplete: mp_n500_k2; fields of the two-slab run
caption: Lid-driven cavity filled with the micropolar fluid: K = 3, Reynolds number 400 on mu_inf (1,000 on mu), l = L / 20 (25 dx at n = 500, 12.5 dx at n = 250), Theta = l^2, w = 0 on the four walls, Ma = 0.01, thesis configuration with the default walls. (a) u on the vertical centre line and (b) v on the horizontal centre line, time means over the last 20 L / U (MLS samples at 1,001 points, every 25th shown): the micropolar run (circles; crosses: n = 250) and two Newtonian runs on the same particles, one with the viscosity mu_inf that the micropolar fluid has far from walls (solid) and one with mu + kappa that it has inside a wall layer (dashed). (c) Micro-rotation and (d) micro-rotation minus half the curl of the velocity at the last step of run `mp_n500`; the second vanishes in the core and marks the wall layers of thickness l. Colour scales end at the 99.5th percentile of the magnitude. Runs: `newtonian_re400_n500`, `newtonian_re250_n500`, `mp_n500`, `mp_n250`; tag `thesis-ch5-rc2`. The micropolar extrema are not between the two Newtonian ones where the ordering of the viscosities would put them: u_min is beyond the Reynolds-400 value by 0.64 of the distance between the two bounds, v_max beyond the Reynolds-400 value by 0.31 of the distance between the two bounds, v_min beyond the Reynolds-400 value by 0.08 of the distance between the two bounds; the kinetic energy is beyond the Reynolds-400 value by 2.10 of the distance between the two bounds. Along the centre lines the micropolar profile leaves the band of the two bounds at 54 % (u) and 65 % (v) of the points, by at most 5.3e-02 and 4.5e-02 U. The positions of the three extrema do lie between those of the two bounds. N = 250 minus n = 500: rms difference of the centre lines 3.0e-03 (u) and 3.5e-03 (v) U, extrema -5.3e-03, +5.0e-03, -6.1e-03 U (standard error of the time means 2e-05). No reference table for Reynolds number 400 is in the repository (the Marchi et al. files hold 1,000, 3,200 and 5,000), so the Newtonian bound at 400 is not compared with a reference here.
